question: After giving a 10 percent discount on an article there is still a profit of 10 percent. What will be the profit percentage when no discount is given?
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] **__Shortcut Trick__**

CPover MP = 100 - Discountover 100 + Profit = 100 - 10 over100+ 10 = 90over110

⇒ Profit = 20 

⇒ %Profit = 20over90 × 100 = 200over9 = 22.22%

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__** 

**Given:**

After giving a 10 percent discount on an article there is still a profit of 10 percent.

**Formula used:**

SP = MP( {frac{{100 - discount}}{{100}}} ) 

**Calculation:**

Let the Marked Price of the article be 100

Discount = 10%

SP = 100( {frac{{100 - 10}}{{100}}} ) = 90 

Still, there is a profit of 10%

So,

CP = 90× frac{{100}}{{100 + 10}} = 90 × frac{{100}}{{110}} =(900)/(11) 

If no discount was given

Profit = frac{{200 - 120}}{{120}} × 100\% = frac{{80}}{{120}} × 100\% 

**Profit = 22.22%**
